best_for: Households, schools and small offices that want a full office suite at no cost and can live with the odd layout difference in Word and Excel files.
description:
LibreOffice is an office suite from The Document Foundation, a nonprofit, and hundreds of contributors around the world. It grew out of OpenOffice.org and is the most actively developed project to carry that work on. The foundation pitches it as private, with no AI forced on you.

Writer handles anything from a quick note to a full-length book, and Draw goes as far as 3D illustrations. In Math you can build a formula with the visual editor or type it as plain text. Each app has its own guide book linked from the LibreOffice site, and the site also offers templates and extensions. The community works to translate the suite into the world's languages.

points.title: Six apps in one install
points.text: You get Writer for documents, Calc for spreadsheets, Impress for slides, Draw for diagrams, Base for databases and Math for formulas, all at no cost.

points.title: Base needs Java
points.text: Most of the suite runs without Java, but Base needs a Java runtime on every platform. On macOS a full JDK is required, because a plain JRE is not detected.

points.title: Light on hardware
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 or Server 2012 and up, 256 MB of RAM and up to 1.5 GB of disk. macOS 11 or later on Intel or Apple silicon is required. Linux needs kernel 4.18, glibc 2.27 and an x86-64-v2 CPU for the official builds.

points.title: No support contract from the foundation
points.text: The Document Foundation gives no technical support for the free download; help comes from forums and mailing lists. It recommends that schools and large organizations buy LibreOffice Enterprise versions from partner companies for long-term support.

points.title: MSI installers for every Windows PC
points.text: Windows builds come as MSI packages for 32-bit, 64-bit and Arm64, and installing needs administrator rights.

points.title: Two stable lines at once
points.text: The download page lists 26.8 as the latest stable release and still offers 26.2 next to it, plus test builds of 27.2. Office managers can stay on the older line while the newer one settles.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 24 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need the project's archive. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by The Document Foundation.
